doc.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Warren Vache record 'Horn of Plenty'
summary: Monk plays a recent session; Wyands recalls it only vaguely.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Do you listen to your records at home?
Sometimes. But I’m not — sometimes I listen to them in the car but —
This is swinging man. With Warren Vache.
Yeah. It’s called “Horn of Plenty.” Does that ring a bell now? Okay.
I’m trying to think who’s playing saxophone.
I can’t remember. Houston Person I think.
Yeah I think so and Joel Helleny. Does it make you want to go listen to it?
That was a pretty good record. Is “I Can’t Get Started” on that?
I believe so. I believe there’s “Struttin’ with some Barbecue” on that. A nice session.
It did turn out pretty good.
